title: ORCA: Orthogonal Residual Consensus Alignment for Multi-View Clustering
claim: A multi-stage system extracts non-redundant consensus from multiple views, then aligns hierarchical representations against it for clustering.
layout: 3 stacked bands, top-to-bottom and left-to-right, dashed sub-stage boxes
description: A wide architecture diagram in three horizontal bands. The top band shows per-view inputs X1..Xm passing through blue trapezoid encoders to latents Z1..Zm. A purple box labeled reconstruction-loss pre-training points at the encoders. The middle band is the SIRF module. Stage 1 uses colored boxes for primary-view orthogonal projection, with a small 3D vector sketch and a plus node, and outputs augmented Z_aug. Stage 2 has a cross-attention diagram, a KL-divergence halting diamond, a feedback loop and an orange cube output, Z_final. The bottom band is the CCHA module. Z_final and other representations pass through colored MLP icons to H, R_flow, R_view and R_pair. They then go to attention-based weight computation and a multi-scale contrastive loss L_ccha, and finally to a scatter plot of clusters. Pastel fills and dashed rounded borders group the components.
caption: Overview of the proposed ORCA framework, consisting of three main components: (i) View-specific Autoencoders for latent feature extraction; (ii) The SIRF module, which extracts complementary residuals to distill a non-redundant global consensus $H$; and (iii) The CCHA module, which adaptively aligns multi-scale representations (view-level, local, and recurrent) against the global consensus anchor.
abstract: Deep multi-view clustering often suffers from redundant information accumulation during fusion and indiscriminate alignment across representation levels. We propose Orthogonal Residual Consensus Alignment (ORCA) to address these challenges. Its semantic incremental recurrent fusion module extracts cross-view orthogonal residuals as non-redundant increments and adaptively weights recurrent states through divergence-guided gating. Its consensus-calibrated hierarchical contrastive alignment module uses the global consensus to weight contrastive alignment of view-level, pairwise, and recurrent representations. Together, these modules balance view-specific structure with cross-view consistency. Experiments on five benchmarks against fifteen competing methods demonstrate ORCA's effectiveness, including a 5.25 percent accuracy improvement over the strongest baseline on 100leaves. Ablation studies validate both modules. Code is available at https://github.com/XiaojianDing/2026-NeurIPS-ORCA.
